reasoning: According to records from the Congressional Research Service (CRS) and the Pew Research Center, the U.S. Congress has enacted all of its regular annual appropriations bills on time prior to the start of the fiscal year (October 1) only four times since the modern budgeting process was established by the Congressional Budget Act of 1974: for Fiscal Years 1977, 1989, 1995, and 1997. Since FY 1997 (which was passed in September 1996), Congress has consistently failed to pass a complete set of regular spending bills on time, relying instead on stopgap continuing resolutions (CRs) or late omnibus spending packages.
title: US Congress passed no budget on time since 1997
